introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: A polythene rod charged by rubbing with dry cloth is brought close to but not touching a metallic sphere placed on an insulating stand.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Name one other method used in charging a material. *[1 mark]*

(ii) What type of charge is stored on the polythene rod? *[1 mark]*

(iii) Explain why the rod would not have been charged if the cloth was wet. *[2 marks]*

(iv) Explain with the aid of diagrams how the metallic sphere can be made to acquire a positive charge. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Charging by **induction** (or by **contact/conduction**, by touching a charged body to the material).

(ii) **Negative charge.** Rubbing polythene with a cloth transfers electrons to the polythene, which therefore has an excess of electrons.

(iii) Water is a conductor of electricity (it contains dissolved ions). If the cloth is wet, the charge produced by rubbing **leaks away** through the water, to the hand and to the earth, as quickly as it forms, so no charge builds up on the rod.

(iv) **Charging by induction** (three steps, one small diagram each):

1. *Diagram 1:* the negative rod is held near the sphere (not touching). Free electrons in the sphere are repelled to the **far side**, which becomes negative, leaving the **near side positive**.
2. *Diagram 2:* with the rod still in place, **earth the sphere** by touching it with a finger (or joining it to the earth with a wire). Electrons from the far side flow to the earth, leaving the sphere with a net positive charge.
3. *Diagram 3:* remove the earth connection **first**, then remove the rod. The remaining positive charge spreads evenly over the sphere: **the sphere is now positively charged.**
